question.text: Consider the following two binary relations on the set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mo>:</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators="|"><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="}" separators="|"><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math>, then :

options.text: <math><msub><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is symmetric but it is not transitive
<math><msub><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>  is not symmetric but it is transitive

solution.text:
Since, (b, c)∈R1 but (c, b)∉R1 

Hence, R1 is not symmetric.

In R1 : b, c∈R1 and c, a∈R1 but b, a∉R1

So, R1 is not transitive.

R2 is symmetric.

In R2 : b, a∈R2 and a, c∈R1 but b, c∉R2

So, R2 is not transitive.
